facts.fact: The StackAdapt blog post on 3D creative formats was published on June 26, 2020.
Three-dimensional (3D) objects and landscapes can be embedded into HTML5 rich media banners.
facts.quote: Three-dimensional (3D) objects and landscapes can now be embedded into HTML5 rich media banners

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that 3D ad creatives are supported by Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.
facts.quote: is now highly functional across all devices and supported by Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that mobile and desktop devices now have the computational power to render 3D objects in real time, with little to no latency in upload speed.
facts.quote: render 3D objects in real-time resulting in little to no latency in upload speed

facts.fact: StackAdapt says an architect designing in Rhino can export work as an OBJ file that can be embedded into an HTML5 banner.
facts.quote: an architect designing in Rhino can easily export their work as an OBJ file which can then be embedded into an HTML5 banner

facts.fact: StackAdapt cites Shopify and Sketchfab studies as showing that 3D ads can increase return on ad spend by improving CTR, engagement, conversions, and time on site. No figures are given.
facts.quote: have completed studies that have shown that 3D ads are great for brands that are looking to elevate their creatives

facts.fact: StackAdapt describes a planned 3D 'configurator' feature that lets users customize product specs and preview options such as colours.
facts.quote: Users will be able to experiment with different specs, customizing the product to their liking.

facts.fact: StackAdapt describes a 'swirl' 3D functionality designed for mobile, in which the 3D model is tied to the webpage and animates as the user scrolls.
facts.quote: A functionality specifically designed for mobile. As a user scrolls down a webpage, the 3D model is tied to the page and will animate as the user scrolls up and down.
